Inferior shoulder dislocation: 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

After a hyperabduction injury, a patient arrives with the arm fixed overhead and is unable to bring it comfortably to the side. Imaging shows the humeral head below the glenoid. Which dislocation pattern is present?

  1. Inferior shoulder dislocation
  2. Anterior shoulder dislocation
  3. Posterior shoulder dislocation
  4. Acromioclavicular separation
  5. Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Inferior shoulder dislocation

Luxatio erecta places the humeral head below the glenoid, often with the arm fixed overhead.

Understanding the options

Inferior shoulder dislocation
Luxatio erecta places the humeral head below the glenoid, often with the arm fixed overhead.
Anterior shoulder dislocation
Anterior glenohumeral displacement often follows abduction and external rotation and places the head anterior to the glenoid. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Posterior shoulder dislocation
Posterior dislocation may follow seizures or electrical injury and can present with fixed internal rotation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Acromioclavicular separation
AC injury disrupts the clavicle-acromion relationship while the humeral head may remain normally located. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation
Posterior medial clavicular displacement threatens mediastinal structures and warrants urgent specialist care. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
